Neighborhood street main
Hydrant lateral
Service main

question: What is a dead end in a distribution system?
correctAnswer: A main end not tied to another main, fed from one direction
explanation: A dead-end main is fed from only one side. Water in it moves only as customers draw it, which matters for quality and for fire flow.
options: A valve that has been closed during a repair
A pipe that has been abandoned and drained
A main end not tied to another main, fed from one direction
A point where two mains meet and flow splits in half
optionA: A valve that has been closed during a repair
optionB: A pipe that has been abandoned and drained
optionC: A main end not tied to another main, fed from one direction
optionD: A point where two mains meet and flow splits in half

question: What is the main hydraulic advantage of a looped grid over a branched layout?
correctAnswer: Water can reach a point from more than one direction
explanation: In a loop, flow divides between paths and a break can be bypassed. Looping does not create pressure on its own, and elevation still decides whether pumping is needed.
options: Pumps are no longer needed in a loop
Water can reach a point from more than one direction
Pressure rises in each pipe that forms the loop, since flow is shared
Smaller pipes can carry the demand at a higher velocity in a loop
optionA: Pumps are no longer needed in a loop
optionB: Water can reach a point from more than one direction
optionC: Pressure rises in each pipe that forms the loop, since flow is shared
optionD: Smaller pipes can carry the demand at a higher velocity in a loop

question: Why do dead-end mains often produce taste, odor or discolored-water complaints?
correctAnswer: Water sits long, so disinfectant fades and solids settle out
explanation: Low demand at a dead end means long residence time. The disinfectant residual decays and solids drop out, so the water ages.
options: Water moves so fast that it scours the wall clean
Water sits long, so disinfectant fades and solids settle out
The pipe material dissolves faster near the end of a long line
Pressure at the end of the line is high and shakes deposits loose
optionA: Water moves so fast that it scours the wall clean
optionB: Water sits long, so disinfectant fades and solids settle out
optionC: The pipe material dissolves faster near the end of a long line
optionD: Pressure at the end of the line is high and shakes deposits loose

To measure the flow passing through each loop of the grid

question: A valve on a loop is found closed by mistake and left that way. What is the likely effect on the area it serves?
correctAnswer: It behaves like a dead end, with older water and weaker fire flow
explanation: A closed loop valve removes the second path, so flow reaches the area from one side only. Quality and available fire flow both suffer.
options: It behaves like a dead end, with older water and weaker fire flow
The valve acts as a check valve and protects the loop from surges
Water is rerouted so that quality improves in the area behind the valve
Pressure doubles in the closed portion of the loop, which then gets more flow
optionA: It behaves like a dead end, with older water and weaker fire flow
optionB: The valve acts as a check valve and protects the loop from surges
optionC: Water is rerouted so that quality improves in the area behind the valve
optionD: Pressure doubles in the closed portion of the loop, which then gets more flow

correctAnswer: Flow splits between paths, lowering velocity and friction loss
explanation: With two paths feeding a hydrant, each carries part of the flow. Lower velocity means less head loss, leaving more pressure at the hydrant.
options: Flow splits between paths, lowering velocity and friction loss
Loops hold a larger stored volume than branches can hold
Friction loss does not occur in a pipe that is part of a loop
Looped pipes have a larger internal diameter than branched pipes do
optionA: Flow splits between paths, lowering velocity and friction loss
optionB: Loops hold a larger stored volume than branches can hold
optionC: Friction loss does not occur in a pipe that is part of a loop
optionD: Looped pipes have a larger internal diameter than branched pipes do

To make the pipe walls thicker so it needs no outer coating at all
To let the pipe bend around curves with no fittings at all

Both metals corrode at the same slow rate
The more active metal tends to corrode faster
The less active metal tends to corrode faster than before

A rubber gasket squeezed between spigot and bell
A lead and oakum packing driven into the bell by hand

Soil expands around fittings and squeezes the joints apart
Water hammer occurs at fittings and loosens bolts on the line

Undisturbed soil bonds chemically to the concrete poured on it
Loose soil gives way under the thrust load
Backfill would crack the concrete as it dries out over time

question: Why is backfill placed and compacted in layers around and above a pipe?
correctAnswer: To support the pipe and prevent later settling
explanation: Layered, compacted backfill supports the pipe and surface above it. Dumping soil at once can leave voids that settle later or damage the pipe.
options: To support the pipe and prevent later settling
To warm the pipe so that it can expand in the trench
To make the trench look neat when the job is finished
To keep the gaskets from drying out while buried
optionA: To support the pipe and prevent later settling
optionB: To warm the pipe so that it can expand in the trench
optionC: To make the trench look neat when the job is finished
optionD: To keep the gaskets from drying out while buried

question: When a repaired main is put back in service, why are the valves opened slowly while air is vented?
correctAnswer: To avoid trapped air and pressure surges
explanation: Filling too fast pushes pockets of air along the pipe and can create strong surges. A slow fill with venting lets the air out and the pipe fill smoothly.
options: To keep the meters on the line from turning during the fill
To avoid trapped air and pressure surges
To stop the pressure from reaching its normal value
To let the chlorine form properly inside of the pipe
optionA: To keep the meters on the line from turning during the fill
optionB: To avoid trapped air and pressure surges
optionC: To stop the pressure from reaching its normal value
optionD: To let the chlorine form properly inside of the pipe

question: Why is a temporary connection that fills a main being disinfected from a live main usually fitted with backflow protection?
correctAnswer: To keep chlorinated or dirty water from returning into the live system
explanation: If pressure in the live main drops while filling, the water in the new main or hose could be drawn back. Protection keeps it from reaching customers.
options: To let the new main be tested at a much higher pressure
To keep chlorinated or dirty water from returning into the live system
To check the pressure at the hydrant that is used for filling
To raise the flow into the new main from the live one
optionA: To let the new main be tested at a much higher pressure
optionB: To keep chlorinated or dirty water from returning into the live system
optionC: To check the pressure at the hydrant that is used for filling
optionD: To raise the flow into the new main from the live one

question: What does static pressure describe in a distribution main?
correctAnswer: The pressure in the water while it is standing still
explanation: Static pressure is the pressure of standing water, set mainly by the height of water above the point. It does not include any loss from movement.
options: The pressure lost to friction along a long main
The pressure a pump makes at its best efficiency point
The pressure at a hydrant while it discharges wide open
The pressure in the water while it is standing still
optionA: The pressure lost to friction along a long main
optionB: The pressure a pump makes at its best efficiency point
optionC: The pressure at a hydrant while it discharges wide open
optionD: The pressure in the water while it is standing still

Their water travelled a shorter distance
The water column above them is taller
Gravity empties the pipes on the hills

question: How does pressure at a point in a main usually compare when customers are drawing heavily with when there is no draw?
correctAnswer: It is lower during heavy draw because friction uses up some head
explanation: Flow brings friction loss, so some of the available head is spent moving the water and the pressure at the point drops.
options: It is higher at first and then falls to the static value
It is lower during heavy draw because friction uses up some head
It is equal, since the tank level sets pressure
It is higher during heavy draw because moving water pushes harder
optionA: It is higher at first and then falls to the static value
optionB: It is lower during heavy draw because friction uses up some head
optionC: It is equal, since the tank level sets pressure
optionD: It is higher during heavy draw because moving water pushes harder

explanation: A single grade would overpressure low ground or starve high ground. Zones hold pressures in a workable range for everyone.
options: Elevation differences would give very high pressure low and poor pressure high
Each zone can then use a different brand of meter and register type
Zones reduce the total miles of main that a utility must own
Zones keep chlorine levels equal across the whole service area
optionA: Elevation differences would give very high pressure low and poor pressure high
optionB: Each zone can then use a different brand of meter and register type
optionC: Zones reduce the total miles of main that a utility must own
optionD: Zones keep chlorine levels equal across the whole service area

Morning demand raises friction loss on the supply route
The elevation of the house changed after sunrise

By multiplying flow area by water velocity
By multiplying velocity by the pressure head
By multiplying pipe length by system pressure

correctAnswer: Water rubbing on the pipe wall and on itself as it moves
explanation: Moving water meets resistance from the wall and from internal turbulence, which turns head into lost energy.
options: Small air bubbles that collect in the line
Water cooling down as it travels through the main
Water rubbing on the pipe wall and on itself as it moves
The weight of the water column pressing on the pipe
optionA: Small air bubbles that collect in the line
optionB: Water cooling down as it travels through the main
optionC: Water rubbing on the pipe wall and on itself as it moves
optionD: The weight of the water column pressing on the pipe

It rises, so less head is lost
It falls, so more head is lost for the same flow
It stays put because the material is unchanged

question: Where in a chloraminated system is nitrification most likely to be noticed first?
correctAnswer: At far ends and in storage where water age is high
explanation: Nitrification needs time and a falling residual, which are found at remote points and in tanks with poor turnover.
options: Right at the point where the water leaves the plant
In pipes carrying the highest and steadiest flow
At fresh hydrants on a large transmission main
At far ends and in storage where water age is high
optionA: Right at the point where the water leaves the plant
optionB: In pipes carrying the highest and steadiest flow
optionC: At fresh hydrants on a large transmission main
optionD: At far ends and in storage where water age is high

topic: Nitrification in chloraminated systems
question: What can happen to chloramine as it decays, which is relevant to nitrification?
correctAnswer: It can release ammonia that bacteria then use
explanation: As chloramine breaks down, ammonia is released, and in warm old water that ammonia can fuel nitrifying organisms.
options: It can raise the free chlorine at the plant
It can release ammonia that bacteria then use
It can become a mineral scale on the pipe
It can turn into pure chlorine in the main
optionA: It can raise the free chlorine at the plant
optionB: It can release ammonia that bacteria then use
optionC: It can become a mineral scale on the pipe
optionD: It can turn into pure chlorine in the main
